item.title: Pfizer/Arvinas Vepdegestrant (Veppanu) FDA Approval
item.description:
• Summary: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Vepdegestrant (Veppanu), a first-in-class PROTAC estrogen receptor degrader co-developed by Pfizer and Arvinas, for the treatment of certain breast cancers. The decision was based on data from a pivotal trial in patients with ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer who had received prior endocrine therapy. Despite mixed efficacy signals, the agency accepted the risk-benefit profile for accelerated approval. The approval marks a new modality in breast cancer treatment, validating the targeted protein degradation approach.
  • MoAs: Estrogen receptor degradation via PROTAC-mediated ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma, BioPharma Dive, Endpoints News

item.title: AstraZeneca Camizestrant FDA AdCom Setback
item.description:
• Summary: An FDA advisory committee voted against recommending AstraZeneca's selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) Camizestrant for approval in breast cancer. The vote came after a review of data from the SERENA trials, which showed some benefit but raised concerns about overall survival and toxicity. The decision surprises many analysts and poses a setback for AstraZeneca's oncology pipeline. The FDA will consider the committee's input before making a final decision. Camizestrant is designed to target ER+ breast cancer and previously showed promise in earlier-stage trials.
  • MoAs: Selective estrogen receptor degradation (SERD)
  • Sources: ApexOnco, BioSpace

item.title: Summit Ivonescimab Interim Trial Miss
item.description:
• Summary: Summit Therapeutics' Ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, failed to meet interim analysis endpoints in a pivotal trial, surprising analysts and causing shares to tumble. The trial, likely in non-small cell lung cancer, had been closely watched as a potential competitor to checkpoint inhibitors. The miss raises questions about the drug's efficacy and future development pathway. Ivonescimab was designed to simultaneously block immune checkpoint and angiogenesis pathways.
  • MoAs: Bispecific antibody: blockade of PD-1 and VEGF-A
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, Fierce Pharma, ApexOnco, Endpoints News

item.title: J&J Axes CAR-T Therapies
item.description:
• Summary: Johnson & Johnson has discontinued two CAR-T cell therapy programs for lymphoma, a major setback months after touting their efficacy. The decision was driven by an evolving competitive landscape and changing market dynamics. J&J had invested heavily in these autologous CAR-T candidates, which targeted CD19. The discontinuations highlight the challenges in the CAR-T space, including manufacturing complexity and pricing pressures. J&J shifted focus to other oncology assets and next-generation platforms.
  • MoAs: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy targeting CD19
  • Sources: Fierce Biotech, Endpoints News

item.title: Verastem Ovarian Cancer Campaign
item.description:
• Summary: Verastem Oncology launched the "Reimagine" campaign to move its ovarian cancer drugs avutometinib and defactinib into earlier treatment lines. The initiative aims to leverage promising clinical data to shift the standard of care in ovarian cancer.
  • MoAs: Avutometinib: RAF/MEK inhibitor. Defactinib: FAK inhibitor.
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma

item.title: Merck Drops SAC-TMT Program
item.description:
• Summary: Merck quietly discontinued its SAC-TMT antibody-drug conjugate program, a follow-up to other companies' technologies. The decision underscores the competitive challenges in the ADC space and Merck's strategic pipeline pruning.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: ApexOnco
